It holds the entities (User, Project, Task), the status value type and its guard (TaskStatus, TASK_STATUSES, isTaskStatus), a query type (TaskFilter), the domain errors (ValidationError, NotFoundError, ConflictError), one state-transition rule (markDone) and the repository interfaces (UserRepository, ProjectRepository, TaskRepository). Each rule lives in one place. The "already done" check exists only in markDone, and status membership is checked only by isTaskStatus, which uses TASK_STATUSES. The file defines its own abstractions and doesn't bypass any of them; the repository interfaces use only the module's own types. There is one small weakness. The status values are written twice: once in the TaskStatus union and once in the TASK_STATUSES array. The compiler checks each array entry against the union, but it won't catch a status that is left out of the array. Writing the type as `(typeof TASK_STATUSES)[number]` would fix this. It sits in the same file and the compiler partly guards it, so it doesn't count as splitting a rule across places.
